policy_name: Acceptable Use of Artificial Intelligence Technologies (NYS-P24-001)
issuing_authority: New York State Office of Information Technology Services (ITS), Chief Data Office
regulatory_regime: NYS statewide IT policy under State Technology Law §103(10) and Executive Order 117
geo_constraints: New York State Entities (state agencies) and third parties using IT resources administered by an SE or ITS

locale_context.region: North America › United States (New York State)
locale_context.regulation: State government IT policy · mandatory for State Entities, risk-based with NIST AI RMF alignment
locale_context.culture: US state-government administrative governance: enables agency AI adoption while imposing human final decision-making, bias monitoring and public inventory, anchored in the NIST AI RMF rather than statute.

key_dates.event: Policy issued (Revision History); takes effect upon publication

versions.title: NYS-P24-001 issued
versions.summary: First issue of the statewide policy on acceptable use of AI technologies by State Entities.

changes.detail: Applies to AI systems developed, used or procured by SEs that could directly impact the public
Human oversight of decisions; automated final decision systems not permitted
Risk assessment per AI system, bias monitoring, privacy and security controls
Disclosure of AI use to the public; ITS public AI inventory

versions.note: Content of the January 2024 text is not available in this copy; the 'changes' describe the policy as in the 2025 update and assume the core requirements were introduced at first issue.

versions.title: NYS-P24-001 updated
versions.summary: Updated policy (Revision History: 'Updated policy'). The document does not say what changed.
versions.note: Changes from the 2024 issue are not described in the document.

covered_entities: State Entities (State Government under EO 117 / State Agencies under State Technology Law §101)
third parties using SE/ITS-administered IT resources (local governments, consultants, vendors, contractors)
covered_systems: AI systems (incl. machine learning, LLMs, NLP, computer vision, generative AI) that may directly impact the public
covered_activities: development, use and procurement of AI systems by SEs
exceptions: basic calculations, basic automation and rule-based 'if this then that' systems
SEs' regulatory or other actions regarding non-agency uses of AI
exceptions granted by ITS where compliance is not feasible or deviation is needed for a business function
conditions: applies to AI systems that, when used, could 'directly impact the public' (safety, welfare or rights; e.g. law enforcement, housing, hiring, benefits, child welfare, critical infrastructure)
where an SE policy conflicts, the more restrictive policy prevails
objective: Establish rules for State Entities' acceptable use of AI so that agencies can innovate and serve New Yorkers while protecting privacy, managing risk and promoting accountability, safety and equity.
principles: human oversight / no automated final decisions
parent_policy: NYS-P08-002 Authority to Establish State Enterprise IT Policy, Standards and Guidelines

related_policies.policy: ITS-P19-005 Acceptable Use of Open Source Software

conflict_rule: An SE may adopt its own policy but it must include these requirements; where an SE policy conflicts, the more restrictive policy takes precedence (§3.1).

record_provenance.notes: Text taken from the copy in asago-ai/asago-policy-mapper (policy_examples/new-york-state.pdf). The copy is the version updated 03/11/2025; whether a later revision exists was not checked (no web access). Binding=false because this is not law, but compliance is mandatory for State Entities and covered third parties (§5.0, issued under State Technology Law §103(10)). Footnote 4 and section 9.0 'Related Documents' are empty in the copy. Policy id uses the first-issue year (2024, as in the policy number NYS-P24-001).

clauses.original_text: SEs must ensure that decisions that impact the public are not made without oversight by appropriate staff, who make the final decisions. Automated final decision systems are not permitted.
clauses.action: ensure human oversight and final decision by staff
clauses.requirement: no automated final decisions; appropriate staff make final decisions
clauses.purpose: protect the public from unchecked automated decisions
clauses.affected_asset: rights, safety and welfare of the public
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: Second sentence is an outright prohibition (MUST NOT) on automated final decision systems.

clauses.original_text: Use of AI systems must be fair and equitable in accordance with applicable State and Federal laws, rules, and regulations. SE must be aware that systemic, computational, and human biases may impact AI systems and should develop a plan to monitor for such biases, and, where identified, remediated identified biases.
clauses.requirement: fair and equitable use; plan to monitor and remediate biases
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: Fairness itself is MUST; the bias monitoring plan is phrased SHOULD. Wording 'remediated' is as in the document.

clauses.original_text: Where members of the public interact directly with SE systems that use AI technology, the use of such AI technology should be disclosed by the SE. Furthermore, SE users of AI systems must provide meaningful oversight over all decisions made by an AI system and be able to explain the decision or output.
clauses.object: AI systems the public interacts with; AI decisions/outputs
clauses.requirement: disclose AI interaction to the public; be able to explain AI decisions
clauses.condition: where the public interacts directly with an AI-enabled SE system
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: Footnote marker 6 omitted. Disclosure is SHOULD; explainability/oversight is MUST. Footnote 6 example: chatbot users should be made aware they are interacting with a machine.

clauses.original_text: The SE must perform a Risk Assessment for each AI system that meets the criteria set forth in Section 3.2. The Risk Assessment must include a review of all security, privacy, legal, reputational, and competency risks as well as the additional risks listed in this policy.
clauses.requirement: risk assessment covering security, privacy, legal, reputational and competency risks
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: ITS-supported agencies must do this in collaboration with ITS; SEs should adopt the NIST AI RMF and follow NYS-S14-001.

clauses.original_text: SEs must develop polices and controls to ensure the appropriate use of all AI systems (e.g., open-source AI systems, publicly available AI systems), particularly in the limited circumstances when the SE identifies a need to use the AI system to process personally identifiable, confidential, or sensitive information.
clauses.object: use of AI systems processing PII, confidential or sensitive information
clauses.requirement: privacy policies and controls (e.g. PIA, data minimisation, retention, disposal, data-subject transparency)
clauses.condition: particularly where AI processes personally identifiable, confidential or sensitive information
clauses.applicable_systems: all AI systems incl. open-source and publicly available AI
clauses.interpretation_notes: 'polices' is the document's spelling. The listed example controls are illustrative.

clauses.original_text: AI systems must be developed and reviewed in alignment with NYS-S13-001: Secure Systems Development Lifecycle. In addition, SEs must ensure there are adequate security controls including encryption and pseudonymization, where appropriate, depending on the risk throughout the data lifecycle.
clauses.action: apply secure SDLC and security controls
clauses.requirement: secure development lifecycle; encryption and pseudonymisation as appropriate
clauses.applicable_systems: AI systems developed, used or procured by NY State Entities that could directly impact the public
clauses.interpretation_notes: AI systems must also comply with NYS-P03-002, NYS-P14-001 and any additional controls required by law (e.g. IRS Publication 1075).
